category: probability and stochastic processes / stochastic processes
canonical_claim: Let X and Y be centered real Gaussian vectors indexed by the same nonempty finite set. If corresponding coordinates have equal variances and Cov(X_i, X_j) is at most Cov(Y_i, Y_j) for every distinct i and j, then for every real threshold u, P(max_i X_i <= u) is at most P(max_i Y_i <= u).
domain_and_universes: A nonempty finite index type and two finite-dimensional real Gaussian random vectors on probability spaces; exact Lean probability-space encoding remains open.
quantifiers: Index type I; probability-space representations of X and Y; centered joint-Gaussian hypotheses; equal coordinate variances; pairwise covariance order; threshold u : Real.
hypotheses: X and Y are centered jointly Gaussian real vectors
Cov(X_i, X_j) <= Cov(Y_i, Y_j) for every distinct i and j
conclusion: For every real u, P(max_i X_i <= u) <= P(max_i Y_i <= u).
excluded_degenerate_cases: The empty index set is excluded. Singular covariance matrices and repeated or almost-surely equal coordinates are intended to be included, subject to confirmation against the selected primary statement.
